contracts.claim: A durable job keeps its id, receipt path and original request immutable; repeated identical requests reuse their receipt and conflicting requests are rejected.

Completion and interruption remain terminal; blockers preserve actionable evidence until explicit cancellation; cancellation claims and stopped jobs cannot be revived by late worker events. Actual detached start is single-flight under concurrent callers; actual early-cancelled workers return before backend import; positively dead cancelling workers finalize cancelled.

Arming deducts durable startup delay; cancellation and settlement preserve other budget dimensions; exhausted budgets retain their original exhaustion receipt and cancelled jobs release still-active budgets. Verified owned process-tree termination stops descendants; operator cancellation releases active budgets and real deadline cancellation retains exhaustion. Actual owned-child termination denial preserves an armed active budget after failed operator cancellation; real deadline enforcement records retry attempts while denial remains, then stops the child after access restoration before its safety exit. Retry history and unrelated budget dimensions remain durable.
Admission and execution policy limits are integers within retention, may tighten across instances, cannot expand ambiently, and unreadable policies fail closed.
Observed timings and ordered timeline phases derive from durable timestamps; receipts remain unchanged; blocked runs remain nonterminal and every list row has additive metrics.

Serialized admission counts every unresolved, blocked, unknown or unreadable receipt; terminal outcomes release capacity; concurrent creates cannot exceed the durable operator limit. Admission scans beyond the visible hundred-row list; unsupported future terminal schemas survive pruning and consume capacity.

Only the oldest waiting job acquires bounded OS slots; legacy and unreadable active receipts reserve capacity, held and crash-released locks remain authoritative, waiting workers stay running to prohibit duplicate launch.

Mutation uses bounded stable OS guard shards; live old legacy owners and recent malformed compatibility fences remain fail closed, even with a short caller-specific wait; aged tokenized locks serialize until actual guard release, and dead owners recover. Non-destructive Win32 liveness uses observed synchronization waits or ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER=87 as positive death; indeterminate errors retain ownership. Actual owned-child Win32 ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED=5 and unavailable command-line lookup retain live ownership and admission pressure; only that child DACL is temporarily changed, restored through the retained creation handle, and the child is reaped.

Explicit hard runtime budget priority is nested, canonical, then snake-case; booleans, invalid, negative and platform-unsupported timeouts fail closed, malformed persisted startup timestamps expire immediately.
Saved profiles contain only public route fields and credential environment-variable names; unknown raw secret fields never persist.

Gateway overlays preserve exact explicit harness/profile/model/base routing and map runtime credential references into the correct auth surfaces; Claude CLIProxy requires explicit loopback HTTP and a present credential, while Rook derives the exact provider from its key name.
Instruction edits stay within supported workspace files, preserve prior bytes in a recoverable backup and return byte-accurate saved receipts; path escape is rejected.

The canonical current catalog includes all sixteen harnesses including Hermes/OpenClaw with truthful security, transport, public gateway and extension ownership; missing supplied provider configuration remains setup-required, native release probing uses intrinsic evidence and existing home uv-bin discovery remains available.
Valid Grok custom models remain exact; a foreign Claude model requires explicit allow_custom policy and otherwise fails closed.
